section.title: Preface
section.p: This Activities Workbook includes a Lesson for each section of the textbook. The Lessons are intended for use for in class and present the skills of algebra in the context of modeling and problem-solving. There is a pdf version of the workbook that can be printed out for students, with space for their work, and a pretext version of the Instructor's Guide. Besides the Activities, the Instructor's Guide includes objectives for each section, tips for teaching, and questions for writing or discussion.

We have also provided some activity-specific Concept Questions for each Lesson; if you use "clickers" for these questions, Turning Point will grade them and keep the scores for you. If you make them part of the grade, they can help motivate students to focus on the lesson during class time. Alternatively, the Concept Questions questions can be used as part of a review before exams.

subsection.title: Suggested Course Structure
subsection.p: Before coming to class, students should read the assigned section and answer the embedded QuickCheck reading questions. We want students to learn how to read a textbook, rather than relying entirely on an instructor's lecture to provide all the information they need. There is also a Preview set of Homework Problems on the prerequisite skills needed for the section; these can be assigned before class or used as the class opener.

Class time can then be spent primarily on the Activities. You may want to give a brief introduction, but should start on the Activities as soon as possible to allow students sufficient time. Usually, students should work on the Activities in groups of three or four, while you circulate to answer questions and provide support. For some Lessons it may be more effective to lead the class as a whole in a guided inquiry.

Allow time at the end of class for a summary of the Lesson. The Check Your Understanding questions highlight the main points of the Activities. There is also a Wrap-Up that outlines the concepts and skills addressed in the Lesson.
